rules.title: Writ type-literal <type:T>
rules.statement: A Writ value `<type:T>` embeds a Logos type T as a first-class value. T is resolved as a type (primitives, structs, in-scope type-params, and generic instantiations like Vec<u8> all permitted). The value carries (kind, type-uid, canonical-name) where the name is the canonical printed form (e.g. "Vec<u8>") and serves as the value's identity label.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: Writ first-class type values have no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Bare type-name in <type:T> must be a known type or in-scope type-param
rules.statement: When `<type:T>` names a bare type identifier that is neither a resolvable known type nor an in-scope type-param, it is a compile error; the diagnostic directs the user to declare T as a type-param of the enclosing const (`pub const X<T>: WritStatic = ...`) or use a concrete type.

rules.title: <type:CFG.path> at writ-value position
rules.statement: `<type:CFG.path>` resolves the config path eagerly and must denote a concrete top-level alias; if it resolves to a const-generic config-slot parameter (kind CfgSlotType) it is rejected with a compile error (parametric Writ literals are not supported).
rules.uncertainty: Restriction is stated as a current limitation in the source.

rules.title: Writ negative integer literal
rules.statement: A Writ negative-integer node yields an integer Writ value equal to the negation of the parsed decimal magnitude.

rules.title: Writ null literal
rules.statement: A Writ null node yields the null Writ value.

rules.title: Writ bool literal
rules.statement: A Writ bool node yields a boolean Writ value; the value is true iff its byte payload is present and nonzero.

rules.title: Writ integer literal: suffix stripping and radix
rules.statement: A Writ integer literal accepts an optional numeric-type suffix (i8/i16/i24/i32/i56/i64/i128, u8/u16/u24/u32/u56/u64/u128, usize, isize) which is stripped before parsing, an optional leading '-', and a radix prefix: `0x` = hexadecimal, `0b` = binary, otherwise decimal. The resulting magnitude is negated if the sign was present.
rules.divergence: Logos addition (Writ literals); note i24/i56/u24/u56 width suffixes.

rules.title: Writ float literal: suffix stripping
rules.statement: A Writ float literal accepts an optional `f32` or `f64` suffix which is stripped before parsing the value as a double-precision float.

rules.title: Writ string literal: quote stripping and escapes
rules.statement: A Writ string literal has surrounding double-quotes stripped and recognizes escape sequences \n, \t, \r, \\, \", \0; an unrecognized escape `\x` is kept literally as backslash followed by x.
rules.divergence: Logos addition (Writ literals); escape set is a fixed subset.

rules.title: Writ map literal keys (string or integer)
rules.statement: An untyped Writ map `@{...}` has entries whose key is either a quoted string (quote-stripped and escape-processed like a Writ string) or an integer; an integer key is negated when the entry carries the negative-key marker. Values are recursively lowered Writ values.

rules.title: Writ untyped array literal
rules.statement: An untyped Writ array `@[...]` lowers each element as a recursive Writ value in order.

rules.title: Typed Writ array element types
rules.statement: A typed Writ array `@<E>[...]` requires E to be one of I8, U8, I16, U16, I32, U32, I64, U64, F32, F64; any other element type is a compile error.

rules.title: Typed Writ arrays reject $-captures
rules.statement: Within a typed Writ array `@<E>[...]`, a $-capture element ($ident or $expr) is a compile error because typed arrays store raw element values rather than AnyVal; an untyped `@[...]` literal must be used instead.

rules.title: @<I32> array element range check
rules.statement: Each integer element of an `@<I32>[...]` typed array is bounds-checked at compile time to the i32 range [-2147483648, 2147483647]; out-of-range values are a compile error.

rules.title: Typed Writ map key/value types
rules.statement: A typed Writ map `@<K>{...}` or `@<K,V>{...}` requires K ∈ {I32, U32, I64, U64, Varchar} and, if V is given, V == AnyVal; any other key or value type is a compile error. Varchar keys produce the same representation as the untyped object map.

rules.title: Typed integer-map key discipline
rules.statement: In a typed integer-keyed Writ map, a string key is a compile error (integer maps require integer keys); integer keys are negated when marked negative, and are bounds/sign-checked per key type: I32 to [-2^31, 2^31-1], U32 to [0, 2^32-1], U64 to non-negative.

rules.title: $-capture only inside capturable @-literal
rules.statement: A $-capture ($ident or $expr) in a Writ value is a compile error unless it occurs inside a capturable @-literal context.

rules.title: Types capturable by $-capture into a Writ value
rules.statement: A captured Logos expression is admissible into a Writ @-literal iff its type is: a scalar integer (i8/i16/i32/i64/u8/u16/u32/u64) or bool (coerced to inline AnyVal); F32/F64/float-literal (zone-allocated F64); AnyVal or a string-view struct; a pointer to u8 (*const u8 / *mut u8, captured as C-string varchar); or a u8 slice (str/&[u8], captured as varchar with length). Other types are not capturable.
